title: [Run] Improve error message for file not found
author: enricogior
summary: PowerToys Run still offers malformed or nonexistent Windows file paths through the URI Handler and then shows a generic failure dialog when launch fails.
next_action: Approve a narrow design that excludes Windows drive/file paths from URI Handler results while preserving real URLs, application URIs, and UNC handling.

confidence.rationale: The current source directly confirms the permissive validator and the original input establishes the undesired result.

judgment.rationale: The original crash is fixed, but current source still accepts every parsed URI host and a contributor has identified the exact validation boundary and requested scope direction.
evidence: Issue #9911 confirms the crash became a generic URI Handler error and this issue was opened for the remaining UX defect.
A prospective contributor identified drive-letter paths falling into the URI result and proposed focused MSTest coverage.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a narrow design that excludes Windows drive/file paths from URI Handler results while preserving real URLs, application URIs, and UNC handling.

fix_assessment.rationale: No current fix is linked, and the validation boundary remains permissive in main.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys Run still offers malformed or nonexistent Windows file paths through the URI Handler and then shows a generic failure dialog when launch fails.
known_information: The original input is a nonexistent Windows drive-letter path offered as `open in browser`.
The crash itself was fixed in PowerToys 0.33.1.
Current UriResolver host validation does not reject any parsed value.
inferences: Filtering file-shaped input before result creation should prevent the misleading action without changing the generic error path for valid URIs that later fail.
issue_context.analysis: The source and history support the contributor's first scope option; changing only the dialog would retain a misleading result for input owned by file-system plugins.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live issue and the full predecessor discussion in #9911.
Fetched current `src/modules/launcher/Plugins/Microsoft.Plugin.Uri/UriHelper/UriResolver.cs` and confirmed `IsValidHost` returns true.

actions.label: Approve URI file-path filtering design
actions.design_summary: Reject drive-letter and other file-system-shaped inputs before URI Handler result creation, preserve supported URL/application URI schemes and UNC ownership, and add focused resolver/query tests.
actions.note: Approval would start a separate fork-side design workflow; this lightweight pass writes no code or upstream content.

proposed_fixes.title: Exclude Windows file paths from URI Handler results
proposed_fixes.root_cause: `UriResolver.IsValidHost` currently accepts every parsed URI, allowing nonexistent drive-letter paths to be presented as browser-launchable URIs and fail through a generic dialog.
plan: Define URI Handler ownership rules that reject drive-letter and file-system path shapes while preserving supported web and application URI schemes.
Apply the rule before producing the URI Handler result so invalid file paths are not offered as `open in browser`.
Add MSTest cases for the original nonexistent path, valid HTTPS and application URIs, and UNC inputs so the Folder plugin remains authoritative for shares.
verification: Query the original nonexistent drive-letter path from issue #9911 and confirm no URI Handler result appears.
Confirm valid HTTPS and registered application URIs still launch and UNC paths are not misrouted to the browser.

confidence.rationale: The permissive current method and original failure path are directly documented; scheme allow-list details remain an implementation choice.
